evidence.source: Main paper structural definition and Table 1: complex 1 is the Br compound C13H16BrCuN3OS with cell a=6.0003, b=21.1415, c=12.3189 Å; complex 2 is the Cl compound C13H16ClCuN3OS with cell a=5.999, b=21.072, c=12.373 Å.

Main paper crystallographic prose assigns CCDC 2453268 to 1 and 2453269 to 2; this record-number order conflicts with the deposited CIF identities and is treated as a source mapping error, not as a change to complexes 1/2.
Supplied immutable CIF ccdc_2453268.cif: internal archive ID CCDC 2453268, formula C13 H16 Cl Cu N3 O S, and cell a=5.999, b=21.072, c=12.373 Å identify it as paper complex 2 (Cl).
Supplied immutable CIF ccdc_2453269.cif: internal archive ID CCDC 2453269, formula C13 H16 Br Cu N3 O S, and cell a=6.0003, b=21.1415, c=12.3189 Å identify it as paper complex 1 (Br).
Main paper, DFT studies: neutral N and anionic N+1 geometries are optimized and fk+ is defined by atomic charges.
Main paper, experimental DFT section: B3LYP/6-311G calculations and finite-difference Fukui workflow.
Main paper, DFT section: fk+ = qk(N) − qk(N+1).
Main paper Table 4: Cu fk+ values 0.0182 (1, Br) and 0.0299 (2, Cl); values remain attached to complex labels rather than the erroneous prose record-number order.
Main paper theoretical investigation: Cu fk+ in 2 is substantially higher and binding interaction is described as stronger.
Main paper abstract: complexes catalyze oxidation of 3,5-DTBC to 3,5-DTBQ and 2 is more active.
